title: Linear Algebra for Machine Learning
description: Mixed-format quiz (MCQ, true/false, select-all) on scalars, vectors, matrices, matrix operations, why matrix multiplication is fundamental to neural networks, the dot product, and systems of linear equations — aligned with the university question bank (Q11–Q15).

questions.question: What is a scalar in the context of linear algebra for ML?
options: A single numerical value that has magnitude but no direction
An ordered list of numbers
A rectangular grid of numbers arranged in rows and columns
A type of loss function
questions.answer: A single numerical value that has magnitude but no direction

questions.question: What is a vector, in the context of linear algebra?
options: An ordered list of numbers, such as [170, 65, 24]
A single numerical value only
A rectangular grid of numbers in rows and columns
A probability distribution over outcomes
questions.answer: An ordered list of numbers, such as [170, 65, 24]

questions.question: What is a matrix, in the context of linear algebra?
options: A rectangular grid of numbers arranged in rows and columns
A single numerical value
An unordered collection of unique numbers
A function that squashes input into a range between 0 and 1
questions.answer: A rectangular grid of numbers arranged in rows and columns

questions.question: When an entire dataset is represented as a matrix, what do its rows and columns typically represent?
options: Rows are individual records/observations, and columns are features
Rows are model weights, and columns are biases
Rows are labels only, and columns are irrelevant
Rows are activation functions, and columns are loss values
questions.answer: Rows are individual records/observations, and columns are features

questions.question: What does the transpose of a matrix, written A^T, do?
options: Swaps its rows and columns
Multiplies every element by negative one
Deletes every element below the main diagonal
Adds a row of biases to the matrix

questions.question: Which matrix operation combines rows of one matrix with columns of another, multiplying and summing corresponding values to produce each output entry?
options: Matrix multiplication
Scalar multiplication
Elementwise addition
Transposition

questions.question: For a matrix A with dimensions (m × n) multiplied by a matrix B with dimensions (n × p), what are the dimensions of the resulting product AB?
options: m × p
n × n
m × n
p × m

questions.question: Why is matrix multiplication described as fundamental to neural networks?
options: It efficiently computes the weighted sum of inputs for an entire layer at once, instead of one connection at a time
It is used only for loading raw data files into memory
It completely replaces the need for activation functions
It is always slower than computing each connection individually
questions.answer: It efficiently computes the weighted sum of inputs for an entire layer at once, instead of one connection at a time

questions.question: How is the dot product of two vectors calculated?
options: Multiply corresponding elements of the two vectors and sum the results into a single number
Subtract the corresponding elements of the two vectors
Stack the two vectors on top of each other to form a matrix
Take the average of every element in both vectors
questions.answer: Multiply corresponding elements of the two vectors and sum the results into a single number

questions.question: A large positive dot product between two vectors generally indicates that the vectors:
options: Point in a broadly similar direction
Are exactly perpendicular to each other
Point in broadly opposite directions
Have no relationship to each other's direction
questions.answer: Point in a broadly similar direction

questions.question: In a single artificial neuron, the predicted output is calculated as:
options: The dot product of the input features and the learned weights, plus a bias term
The transpose of the input feature vector
The number of training epochs completed so far
The mode of all the input feature values
questions.answer: The dot product of the input features and the learned weights, plus a bias term

questions.question: In linear regression, a system of linear equations Ax = b is used, where x represents:
options: The unknown model parameters (weights) being solved for
Only the known input feature values
The final computed loss value
The number of layers in the model
questions.answer: The unknown model parameters (weights) being solved for

questions.question: Matrix multiplication is the same operation as multiplying two matrices element by element.
options: True
False

questions.question: Every entry of a matrix product AB is itself computed as a dot product between one row of A and one column of B.
options: True
False

questions.question: Because real datasets usually have far more data points (equations) than unknowns, and the points never lie perfectly on a line due to noise, ML typically reframes the problem as minimizing overall error rather than solving the system exactly.
options: True
False

questions.question: Matrix inversion is always fast, numerically stable, and never causes computational problems in machine learning.
options: True
False

questions.question: Which of the following are common matrix operations used in Machine Learning?
options: Addition and subtraction
Scalar multiplication
Matrix multiplication
Randomly shuffling the matrix's columns

questions.question: Which of the following are true about scalars, vectors, and matrices?
options: A vector is a one-dimensional, ordered list of numbers
A matrix is a two-dimensional grid of numbers
A scalar has both magnitude and direction
In deep learning, the weights connecting layers of neurons are stored in matrices
answer: A vector is a one-dimensional, ordered list of numbers
A matrix is a two-dimensional grid of numbers
In deep learning, the weights connecting layers of neurons are stored in matrices

questions.question: Which of the following are real applications of the dot product?
options: Calculating the weighted sum of inputs inside a single neuron
Measuring similarity or alignment between two vectors
Calculating a vector's norm (length)
Sorting a list of strings into alphabetical order
answer: Calculating the weighted sum of inputs inside a single neuron
Measuring similarity or alignment between two vectors

questions.question: Which of the following are given as reasons matrix multiplication matters for training modern, large-scale neural networks?
options: It allows many weighted-sum calculations to be performed together, in parallel
GPUs (graphics hardware) are built to accelerate exactly this operation efficiently
It is what makes training very large and deep networks computationally feasible
It removes the need for any loss function during training
answer: It allows many weighted-sum calculations to be performed together, in parallel
GPUs (graphics hardware) are built to accelerate exactly this operation efficiently
It is what makes training very large and deep networks computationally feasible
